previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder, COPD, and hypertension, was admitted after being found unresponsive in a T station with hypoxemia in the 80s on room air. He was started on high-flow oxygen, IV antibiotics, and steroids for suspected COPD exacerbation or pneumonia. His condition improved, and by the next morning, he was saturating well on room air. However, he refused further treatment, declined labs and exams, and insisted on leaving against medical advice before a Section 35 hold could be filed. He demonstrated capacity to make that decision and was discharged home with instructions to seek care if symptoms worsened.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous
